import unicodedata

def display_width(text: str) -> int:
    """
    Return the number of terminal columns required to display the given Unicode string.

    Wide (W) and Fullwidth (F) characters occupy two columns.
    Combining marks (Mn, Me) and format characters (Cf) occupy zero columns.
    All other characters occupy one column.
    """
    width = 0
    for ch in text:
        cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
        if cat in ('Mn', 'Me', 'Cf'):
            # Zero-width characters
            continue
        eaw = unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch)
        if eaw in ('W', 'F'):
            width += 2
        else:
            width += 1
    return width
